grammar.title: Present Simple
grammar.use: Dung cho thoi quen, lich trinh, su that chung.
grammar.signal: usually, often, every day, on Mondays
grammar.toeicExample: The office opens at 8 a.m. every weekday.

grammar.title: Present Continuous
grammar.use: Dung cho hanh dong dang dien ra hoac ke hoach gan.
grammar.signal: now, at the moment, this week
grammar.toeicExample: The workers are installing new lights in the lobby.

grammar.title: Past Simple
grammar.use: Dung cho hanh dong da ket thuc trong qua khu.
grammar.toeicExample: The shipment arrived yesterday afternoon.

grammar.title: Past Continuous
grammar.use: Dung cho hanh dong dang dien ra tai mot thoi diem trong qua khu.
grammar.toeicExample: The receptionist was answering calls when the client arrived.

grammar.title: Present Perfect
grammar.use: Dung cho trai nghiem, ket qua hien tai, hanh dong vua hoan thanh.
grammar.toeicExample: The company has opened three new branches.

grammar.title: Past Perfect
grammar.use: Dung cho hanh dong xay ra truoc mot moc qua khu khac.
grammar.toeicExample: The meeting had started before the director arrived.

grammar.title: Future Forms
grammar.use: Will cho quyet dinh/du doan; be going to cho ke hoach.
grammar.form: S + will + V / S + am/is/are going to + V
grammar.toeicExample: The training session will begin at 9 a.m.

grammar.title: Future Continuous
grammar.use: Dung cho hanh dong se dang dien ra tai mot thoi diem tuong lai.
grammar.signal: at this time tomorrow, by noon tomorrow
grammar.toeicExample: The team will be reviewing applications at 10 a.m. tomorrow.

grammar.title: Subject Verb Agreement
grammar.use: Dong tu phai phu hop voi chu ngu so it hoac so nhieu.
grammar.form: Singular S + V(s/es); Plural S + V
grammar.signal: each, every, either, neither, along with
grammar.toeicExample: Each employee receives a security badge.

grammar.title: Countable and Uncountable Nouns
grammar.use: Phan biet danh tu dem duoc va khong dem duoc de dung many/much, few/little.
grammar.form: many/few + plural noun; much/little + uncountable noun
grammar.signal: many, much, several, a few, a little
grammar.toeicExample: The office needs several chairs and a little extra space.

grammar.title: Articles
grammar.use: Dung a/an cho danh tu so it lan dau; the cho doi tuong da xac dinh.
grammar.form: a/an + singular noun; the + specific noun
grammar.toeicExample: Please send the invoice to an accountant.

grammar.title: Pronouns
grammar.use: Chon dai tu dung vi tri: chu ngu, tan ngu, so huu, phan than.
grammar.toeicExample: Ms. Carter prepared the report herself.

grammar.title: Adjectives and Adverbs
grammar.use: Tinh tu bo nghia danh tu; trang tu bo nghia dong tu, tinh tu hoac ca cau.
grammar.form: adj + noun; verb + adv; adv + adj
grammar.toeicExample: The technician completed the repair quickly.

grammar.title: Comparatives
grammar.use: So sanh hon giua hai nguoi/vat/su viec.
grammar.toeicExample: This printer is more reliable than the old one.

grammar.title: Superlatives
grammar.use: So sanh nhat trong mot nhom.
grammar.signal: the, in the company, of all
grammar.toeicExample: This is the most popular item in the catalog.

grammar.title: Modals
grammar.use: Dung de noi ve kha nang, yeu cau, loi khuyen, nghia vu.
grammar.signal: can, could, should, must, may, might
grammar.toeicExample: Passengers must show a valid ticket before boarding.

grammar.title: Passive Voice
grammar.use: Dung khi tap trung vao vat/nguoi bi tac dong hon la nguoi thuc hien.
grammar.signal: is delivered, was repaired, will be announced
grammar.toeicExample: The conference room was reserved for the marketing team.

grammar.title: Gerunds and Infinitives
grammar.use: Mot so dong tu theo sau boi V-ing, mot so theo sau boi to V.
grammar.toeicExample: The manager decided to postpone the interview.

grammar.title: To Infinitive of Purpose
grammar.use: Dung to V de noi muc dich.
grammar.signal: to reduce costs, to improve service
grammar.toeicExample: The company hired a consultant to improve productivity.

grammar.title: Prepositions of Time
grammar.use: Dung gioi tu thoi gian dung voi ngay, gio, thang, nam.
grammar.form: at + time; on + day/date; in + month/year
grammar.signal: at 9 a.m., on Monday, in June
grammar.toeicExample: The workshop begins at 9 a.m. on Friday.

grammar.title: Prepositions of Place
grammar.use: Mo ta vi tri trong van phong, cua hang, nha ga, khach san.
grammar.form: in, on, at, beside, between, across from
grammar.signal: next to, near, behind, above, below
grammar.toeicExample: The registration desk is across from the elevator.

grammar.title: Coordinating Conjunctions
grammar.use: Noi hai tu, cum tu hoac menh de cung cap do.
grammar.form: and, but, or, so, for, yet
grammar.toeicExample: The hotel is small, but it is close to the station.

grammar.title: Subordinating Conjunctions
grammar.use: Tao menh de phu chi thoi gian, ly do, dieu kien, tuong phan.
grammar.form: because, although, while, if, unless, when
grammar.toeicExample: Although the order was late, the customer accepted it.

grammar.title: Relative Clauses
grammar.use: Dung who/which/that/where de bo sung thong tin cho danh tu.
grammar.toeicExample: The applicant who submitted the resume early was selected.

grammar.title: Noun Clauses
grammar.use: Menh de danh tu lam chu ngu, tan ngu hoac bo ngu.
grammar.toeicExample: The manager explained why the schedule had changed.

grammar.title: Zero and First Conditionals
grammar.use: Zero cho su that chung; first cho dieu kien co the xay ra.
grammar.toeicExample: If the shipment arrives today, we will notify the client.

grammar.title: Second and Third Conditionals
grammar.use: Second cho gia dinh hien tai; third cho gia dinh trai qua khu.
grammar.form: If + past, would + V; If + had V3, would have V3
grammar.toeicExample: If the supplier had shipped earlier, the store would have received the items on time.

grammar.title: Reported Speech
grammar.use: Tuong thuat lai loi noi, thong bao, yeu cau.
grammar.toeicExample: The supervisor said that the policy would change next month.

grammar.title: Question Forms
grammar.use: Tao cau hoi yes/no va wh-question trong giao tiep TOEIC.
grammar.form: Aux + S + V? / Wh + aux + S + V?
grammar.signal: who, what, where, when, why, how
grammar.toeicExample: When will the replacement parts arrive?

grammar.title: Imperatives
grammar.use: Dung de huong dan, yeu cau, canh bao trong thong bao va email.
grammar.signal: please, do not, make sure, remember to
grammar.toeicExample: Please attach the receipt to the form.

grammar.title: Parallel Structure
grammar.use: Cac thanh phan trong danh sach hoac cau so sanh can cung dang ngu phap.
grammar.form: V-ing, V-ing, and V-ing / noun, noun, and noun
grammar.toeicExample: The job requires filing documents, answering calls, and greeting visitors.

grammar.title: Word Forms
grammar.use: Chon dung danh tu, dong tu, tinh tu, trang tu theo vi tri trong cau.
grammar.toeicExample: The manager gave a detailed explanation of the new rule.

grammar.title: Participial Adjectives
grammar.use: Phan biet V-ing va V-ed khi lam tinh tu.
grammar.toeicExample: The instructions were confusing, so several employees asked questions.

grammar.title: Quantifiers
grammar.use: Dung tu chi luong voi danh tu dem duoc va khong dem duoc.
grammar.form: some, any, much, many, a few, a little, enough
grammar.toeicExample: There is enough space in the warehouse for the shipment.

grammar.title: Causative Forms
grammar.use: Noi ve viec nho/yeu cau ai lam gi hoac sap xep dich vu.
grammar.form: have/get + object + V3; have + person + V
grammar.toeicExample: We had the copier repaired yesterday.

grammar.title: Inversion
grammar.use: Dao ngu sau cum phu dinh hoac han che, hay gap o cau trang trong.
grammar.signal: never, rarely, only after, not only
grammar.toeicExample: Only after the contract was signed did production begin.

lines: A: Thanks for joining the contract review meeting.
B: No problem. I read the agreement last night.
A: Good. The supplier must abide by the delivery schedule.
B: I noticed a provision about late shipment fees.
A: Yes, that provision protects both parties.
B: Should we ask for written assurance before we sign?
A: Definitely. We need specific confirmation from their legal team.
B: If there is a cancellation, who pays the administrative fee?
A: The contract says the party that cancels must cover it.
B: Then we should resolve that point before Friday.
A: I will contact the supplier and determine their position.
B: Great. Once they respond, we can establish the final terms.
A: The marketing campaign will launch next month.
B: Have we compared our product with the main competitor?
A: Yes, the report shows our price is more attractive.
B: That should help convince new customers.
A: The current market is crowded, so the message must be clear.
B: Are we using online ads or printed brochures?
A: Both. The online channel should increase traffic quickly.
B: What is the main inspiration for the slogan?
A: We want to focus on customer satisfaction.
B: Good. A productive campaign needs a simple promise.
A: The team will review the banner design tomorrow.
B: I will prepare a short comparison chart for the meeting.
A: Good evening. I have a reservation under Tran.
B: Welcome. May I see your passport and confirmation email?
A: Here they are. Is the room available now?
B: Yes, your double room is ready on the eighth floor.
A: Does the rate include breakfast?
B: Breakfast is complimentary and served in the restaurant.
A: Great. Could I also schedule a wake-up call?
B: Of course. What time would you like the call?
A: Please call me at 6:30 because my departure is early.
B: I have added it to the system.
A: Is there a shuttle to the airport?
B: Yes, the shuttle leaves from the lobby every hour.
A: The copier stopped working during the morning shift.
B: Did you contact technical support?
A: Not yet. I checked the paper tray and the screen first.
B: What does the error message say?
A: It says a component needs maintenance.
B: Then we should call the technician before noon.
A: The supervisor needs copies for the training session.
B: We can use the printer in the accounting department.
A: Good idea. Could you reserve it for thirty minutes?
B: Sure. I will notify the staff by email.
A: Please mention that the copier is temporarily out of service.
B: I will also ask the technician for an estimated repair time.
A: I am calling about shipment number 4082.
B: Let me check the tracking information.
A: The customer expected the package yesterday.
B: It looks like the carrier reported a weather delay.
A: Do we have a new delivery date?
B: The parcel should arrive at the warehouse tomorrow morning.
A: Please notify the customer and apologize for the inconvenience.
B: Should we offer a discount on the shipping fee?
A: Yes, that would be appropriate for this issue.
B: I will update the case number after the call.
A: Also confirm the destination address again.
B: Understood. I will send a follow-up email today.
A: Thank you for coming in for the interview.
B: Thank you for inviting me.
A: Could you briefly describe your previous position?
B: I worked as an office assistant for two years.
A: What duties did you handle most frequently?

readingPassages.title: Contracts practice passage
readingPassages.text: On Monday morning, the contracts team held a short review to prepare for a busy week. The supervisor asked everyone to focus on abide by, agreement, and assurance because these items often appear in daily messages and customer requests. During the meeting, one employee gave an example using cancellation, while another explained how determine could affect the schedule. The team also checked documents related to engage and establish. Before the session ended, the manager assigned a quick exercise with obligate, party, and provision. Everyone had to write two clear sentences and one short email. This practice helped new staff understand the vocabulary in a realistic business situation and prepared them for TOEIC reading questions.
